status.statement: Engineering evidence prepared by a tool; not a subject review. An engineering agent cannot sign this packet.

taskIntent.purpose: Predict, then observe, how a 2×2 matrix M moves the plane: where e₁ and e₂ land (the columns of M), whether orientation is kept or reversed, how areas scale, whether the plane collapses, and which directions stay on their own line.

stages.instruction: Vectors are columns and M acts by M·v. The first column of M is where e₁ = (1, 0) lands and the second column is where e₂ = (0, 1) lands. The grid, the unit square, e₁, e₂, their images and the test vector v are shown; the transformed plane is not shown yet.
The arrows Me₁ and Me₂ are the columns of the matrix shown. Before the transformed plane is shown, predict what M does to the whole plane.

response.prompt: For this matrix, will M keep the counterclockwise order of e₁ and e₂, reverse it, or flatten the plane onto a line or a point? Which directions through the origin, if any, will M map onto their own line?

stages.instruction: Change the matrix entries or type exact values, and watch the transformed grid, the image of the unit square, Mv, the determinant and the area scale. Compare what you see with your prediction.
Now look for directions that M maps onto their own line through the origin. Compare matrices with two such directions, exactly one, every direction, and none.
Explain in your own words how the matrix entries determine orientation, area, collapse and the unchanged directions.

response.prompt: How do the columns of M and its determinant tell you whether orientation is kept or reversed, how areas scale and whether the plane collapses? When does a matrix have no real unchanged direction, exactly one, or every direction?

stages.instruction: Explore freely: change the matrix and the test vector, try the scenarios, and compare the determinant, the area scale and the unchanged directions.

taskFamilies.description: Host-owned prediction request about the orientation, collapse and unchanged directions of a given 2×2 matrix. The host owns the response, its capture and any evaluation.

Host-owned explanation request about how the columns and determinant of a 2×2 matrix determine orientation, area, collapse and unchanged directions. The host owns the response, its capture and any evaluation.
Host-owned later task with a new matrix or a changed representation. Its prompts, held-out items and scoring stay with the host and are not part of this catalogue.

derivation.citation: Derivation written for this catalogue: for v = vx·e₁ + vy·e₂, linearity gives M·v = vx·(M·e₁) + vy·(M·e₂), so the columns of M are the images of e₁ and e₂ and fix the whole map. The image of the unit square is the parallelogram spanned by the columns, with signed area det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21; |det M| scales every area and the sign of det M records whether the counterclockwise order of e₁, e₂ is kept. Eigenvalues are the roots of λ² − (tr M)·λ + det M = 0, real exactly when Δ = (tr M)² − 4·det M ≥ 0; when Δ = 0 and M ≠ λ·I the matrix M − λI has rank 1 and a single eigen-direction. Not independently reviewed.

Study Harness visualizer implementation report §12.2: 2×2 matrix with an explicit column-vector convention, basis vectors, test vector, transformed grid, determinant and nonnegative area when authorized, prediction of orientation, collapse and unchanged directions, and the identity, nonaxis rotation, nonsymmetric shear, reflection, singular collapse, zero matrix and zero vector reference cases.

assumptions: M is a real 2×2 matrix acting linearly on the plane; every statement is about the matrix with exactly the stored entries.
Entries and test-vector components are IEEE-754 double-precision values in [−3, 3]; every value of that range, including 0 and the zero vector, is an allowed experiment.
Orientation, rank and the unchanged-direction category are decided from exact signs and exact equalities for the stored entries, never from a tolerance or from rounded display digits.

Evaluation is deterministic on every conforming JavaScript engine: exact integer arithmetic, IEEE-754 rounding and one correctly rounded square root per unit direction, so the same entries and test vector always give the same values.
limitations: A decimal entry such as 0.7 is stored as the nearest double. A matrix that is singular in decimal arithmetic, such as columns (0.1, 0.3) and (0.7, 2.1), can be invertible as stored, with a determinant near 4e-17; the classification follows the stored values and the determinant shows it. Display rounding is separate from computation.
Rotations by angles other than multiples of 90° have irrational entries; their stored entries are the nearest doubles, so for example det M differs from 1 by about 1e-16.

Rational quantities (images, M·v, determinant, area scale, trace, discriminant, grid and square vertices) are exact and rounded once. Irrational quantities (eigenvalues from a non-square discriminant, unit directions) agree with the exact values to within a few units in the last place.
A nonzero value too small to represent is a numerical-limit (UNDERFLOW) status, never zero; computed subnormal values carry an UNDERFLOW approximation note.
The grid covers only the integer lines −3 ≤ k ≤ 3, and unchanged-direction lines are drawn with half-length 9; both are bounded drawings of unbounded lines.
Only real eigen-directions are drawn. Complex eigenvalues are reported as a status; their rotation-like behaviour is not decomposed.

conventions.coordinate: Column-vector convention: vectors are columns and M acts by M·v. M·e₁ = (m11, m21) is the FIRST COLUMN of M and M·e₂ = (m12, m22) is the second column; entry m_ij is in row i, column j. The plane has x to the right and y up; counterclockwise from +x toward +y is the positive orientation.

m11.label: Matrix entry row 1, column 1
m11.description: Entry m11 of M (row 1, column 1). Column 1 of M is the image M·e1 of the basis vector e1.

m12.label: Matrix entry row 1, column 2
m12.description: Entry m12 of M (row 1, column 2). Column 2 of M is the image M·e2 of the basis vector e2.

m21.label: Matrix entry row 2, column 1
m21.description: Entry m21 of M (row 2, column 1). Column 1 of M is the image M·e1 of the basis vector e1.

m22.label: Matrix entry row 2, column 2
m22.description: Entry m22 of M (row 2, column 2). Column 2 of M is the image M·e2 of the basis vector e2.

vx.label: Test vector x component
vx.description: The x component of the test vector v before the transformation. The zero vector is allowed.

vy.label: Test vector y component
vy.description: The y component of the test vector v before the transformation. The zero vector is allowed.

basis.e1.label: Basis vector e₁
basis.e1.meaning: The standard basis vector e₁ = (1, 0) before the transformation; a fixed reference.
basis.e1.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
basis.e1.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up.

basis.e2.label: Basis vector e₂
basis.e2.meaning: The standard basis vector e₂ = (0, 1) before the transformation; a fixed reference.
basis.e2.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
basis.e2.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up.

vector.v.label: Test vector v
vector.v.meaning: The test vector v = (vx, vy) before the transformation, equal to the stored parameters. It may be the zero vector.
vector.v.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
vector.v.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up.

image.e1.label: Image of e₁
image.e1.meaning: M·e₁ = (m11, m21): the FIRST COLUMN of M (column-vector convention), the point where e₁ lands.
image.e1.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
image.e1.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up.

image.e2.label: Image of e₂
image.e2.meaning: M·e₂ = (m12, m22): the second column of M, the point where e₂ lands.
image.e2.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
image.e2.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up.

image.v.label: Image of v
image.v.meaning: M·v = (m11·vx + m12·vy, m21·vx + m22·vy) = vx·(M·e₁) + vy·(M·e₂), exact and rounded once. It is the zero vector when v = 0 or when v lies along a collapsed direction; the zero vector is a valid result, not an undefined one.
image.v.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
image.v.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up.

determinant.label: Determinant
determinant.meaning: det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21 for the stored entries, exact and rounded once: the signed factor by which M scales areas.
determinant.signConvention: Positive when M keeps the counterclockwise order of e₁ then e₂, negative when it reverses that order, zero when the plane collapses onto a line or a point.

area.scale.label: Area scale
area.scale.meaning: The nonnegative factor |det M| by which M multiplies every area: the area of the image of the unit square. A negative determinant reverses orientation; it never makes an area negative.

orientation.label: Orientation
orientation.meaning: From the exact sign of det M for the stored entries: preserved (det M > 0, the counterclockwise order of e₁ then e₂ is kept), reversed (det M < 0, the order is flipped as by a reflection), collapsed (det M = 0, the plane is flattened onto a line or a point). Never from rounded digits.
orientation.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
orientation.signConvention: Counterclockwise (from +x toward +y) is the positive orientation of the plane.

rank.label: Rank
rank.meaning: Dimension of the image of M, decided exactly for the stored entries: 2 when det M ≠ 0, 1 when det M = 0 and M is not the zero matrix (the plane collapses onto a line), 0 for the zero matrix (every vector maps to the origin).

image.direction.label: Collapse line direction
image.direction.meaning: For rank 1 only: the unit direction of the line through the origin onto which M collapses the plane (the line spanned by the columns of M). Undefined with FULL_RANK for rank 2 (the image is the whole plane) and with ZERO_IMAGE for the zero matrix (the image is a single point).
image.direction.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
image.direction.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up. A line through the origin has two unit directions; the one whose first nonzero component is positive is reported.

trace.label: Trace
trace.meaning: tr M = m11 + m22, exact and rounded once: the sum of the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity, complex ones included).

eigen.discriminant.label: Eigenvalue discriminant
eigen.discriminant.meaning: Δ = (tr M)² − 4·det M = (m11 − m22)² + 4·m12·m21 for the stored entries, exact and rounded once. Δ > 0: two distinct real eigenvalues; Δ = 0: one repeated eigenvalue; Δ < 0: a complex-conjugate pair. Its exact sign decides the eigen category.

eigen.category.label: Unchanged-direction category
eigen.category.meaning: How many directions through the origin M maps onto their own line (M·u = λ·u, with λ possibly negative or zero), decided exactly: two-real (Δ > 0: exactly two such directions), repeated-scalar (M = λ·I: every direction), repeated-defective (Δ = 0 and M ≠ λ·I: exactly one direction), complex (Δ < 0: no real direction). A real matrix does not always have two visible real eigenvectors.

eigen.values.label: Real eigenvalues
eigen.values.meaning: The real eigenvalues (λ₁, λ₂) with λ₁ ≥ λ₂, roots of λ² − (tr M)·λ + det M = 0 listed with multiplicity (a repeated eigenvalue appears twice). Undefined with COMPLEX_EIGENVALUES when Δ < 0. Irrational values agree with the exact roots to within a few units in the last place.
eigen.values.signConvention: A negative eigenvalue reverses vectors along its direction; zero sends that direction to the origin.

eigen.direction1.label: First eigen-direction
eigen.direction1.meaning: A unit vector u₁ with M·u₁ = λ₁·u₁: for two distinct real eigenvalues the direction of λ₁, and for a repeated eigenvalue with M ≠ λ·I the single unchanged direction. Undefined with COMPLEX_EIGENVALUES (no real direction is unchanged) or ALL_DIRECTIONS (M = λ·I: every direction is unchanged, so none is singled out).
eigen.direction1.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
eigen.direction1.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up. A line through the origin has two unit directions; the one whose first nonzero component is positive is reported.

eigen.direction2.label: Second eigen-direction
eigen.direction2.meaning: A unit vector u₂ with M·u₂ = λ₂·u₂ for two distinct real eigenvalues. Undefined with SINGLE_DIRECTION (a repeated eigenvalue with only one unchanged direction), COMPLEX_EIGENVALUES or ALL_DIRECTIONS.
eigen.direction2.coordinateFrame: standard plane: x to the right, y up, origin at the centre
eigen.direction2.signConvention: Components (x, y) in the standard plane, x to the right and y up. A line through the origin has two unit directions; the one whose first nonzero component is positive is reported.

suite.author: Reference cases from the implementation report §12.2 (identity, nonaxis rotation, nonsymmetric shear, reflection, singular collapse, zero matrix, zero vector) and boundary cases added for this catalogue. Values were derived by hand as closed forms and evaluated with plain double arithmetic, except where a case says otherwise; every case is cross-checked against tests/reference/oracles/linear-transformation.ts, an exact rational oracle that shares no code with the catalogue kernel.
suite.review: No independent human subject reviewer has approved these cases. Automated agreement is engineering evidence only.

derivedFrom.conversion: Converted by experiment-kit activity tooling: case IDs, labels, provenance, parameters and tolerances copied unchanged; quantity expectations restated as experiment-kit.reference-fixtures 1.0 expectations.

notCovered: The unit-square image polygon (vertices and degeneracy) is checked by tests/reference/activities/linear-transformation.test.ts.

cases.label: Identity: every vector is unchanged; every direction is an unchanged direction
cases.provenance: hand derivation with the column-vector convention (M·e₁ is the first column): images, det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21, area |det M|, tr M, Δ = (m11 − m22)² + 4·m12·m21, eigenvalues (tr ± √Δ)/2 and null vectors of M − λI; every value is an exact binary fraction; cross-checked exactly against the rational oracle (tests/reference/oracles/linear-transformation.ts)

cases.label: Nonaxis rotation by 30° counterclockwise (irrational entries): area kept, orientation kept, no real unchanged direction
cases.provenance: hand derivation from the exact rotation matrix [[cos θ, −sin θ], [sin θ, cos θ]] (columns are the rotated e₁ and e₂): det = cos²θ + sin²θ = 1, tr = 2 cos θ, Δ = tr² − 4 = −4 sin²θ < 0 so no real eigen-direction; irrational values evaluate the closed forms in double arithmetic. The stored entries are the nearest doubles to √3/2, so values agree with the stored-entry model only within the declared tolerance; cross-checked against the exact rational oracle (tests/reference/oracles/linear-transformation.ts)

cases.label: Nonaxis rotation by 120° counterclockwise (irrational entries): negative trace, still no real unchanged direction
cases.provenance: hand derivation from the exact rotation matrix [[cos θ, −sin θ], [sin θ, cos θ]] (columns are the rotated e₁ and e₂): det = cos²θ + sin²θ = 1, tr = 2 cos θ, Δ = tr² − 4 = −4 sin²θ < 0 so no real eigen-direction; irrational values evaluate the closed forms in double arithmetic. The stored entries are the nearest doubles to √3/2, so values agree with the stored-entry model only within the declared tolerance; cross-checked against the exact rational oracle (tests/reference/oracles/linear-transformation.ts)

The remaining values are hand closed forms of the decimal matrix (directions (1, 3)/√10 and (7, −1)/√50), within the declared tolerance of the stored-entry values

cases.label: Identity: every vector is unchanged; every direction is an unchanged direction
cases.rationale: From reference case identity: hand derivation with the column-vector convention (M·e₁ is the first column): images, det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21, area |det M|, tr M, Δ = (m11 − m22)² + 4·m12·m21, eigenvalues (tr ± √Δ)/2 and null vectors of M − λI; every value is an exact binary fraction; cross-checked exactly against the rational oracle (tests/reference/oracles/linear-transformation.ts)

cases.label: Nonaxis rotation by 30° counterclockwise (irrational entries): area kept, orientation kept, no real unchanged direction
cases.rationale: From reference case rotation-30: hand derivation from the exact rotation matrix [[cos θ, −sin θ], [sin θ, cos θ]] (columns are the rotated e₁ and e₂): det = cos²θ + sin²θ = 1, tr = 2 cos θ, Δ = tr² − 4 = −4 sin²θ < 0 so no real eigen-direction; irrational values evaluate the closed forms in double arithmetic. The stored entries are the nearest doubles to √3/2, so values agree with the stored-entry model only within the declared tolerance; cross-checked against the exact rational oracle (tests/reference/oracles/linear-transformation.ts)

cases.label: Nonaxis rotation by 120° counterclockwise (irrational entries): negative trace, still no real unchanged direction
cases.rationale: From reference case rotation-120: hand derivation from the exact rotation matrix [[cos θ, −sin θ], [sin θ, cos θ]] (columns are the rotated e₁ and e₂): det = cos²θ + sin²θ = 1, tr = 2 cos θ, Δ = tr² − 4 = −4 sin²θ < 0 so no real eigen-direction; irrational values evaluate the closed forms in double arithmetic. The stored entries are the nearest doubles to √3/2, so values agree with the stored-entry model only within the declared tolerance; cross-checked against the exact rational oracle (tests/reference/oracles/linear-transformation.ts)

cases.rationale: From reference case shear-lower: hand derivation with the column-vector convention (M·e₁ is the first column): images, det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21, area |det M|, tr M, Δ = (m11 − m22)² + 4·m12·m21, eigenvalues (tr ± √Δ)/2 and null vectors of M − λI; every value is an exact binary fraction; cross-checked exactly against the rational oracle (tests/reference/oracles/linear-transformation.ts)

cases.label: Symmetric [[1, 1], [1, 0]]: irrational eigenvalues (1 ± √5)/2 with perpendicular unchanged directions
cases.rationale: From reference case golden: hand derivation with the column-vector convention (M·e₁ is the first column): images, det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21, area |det M|, tr M, Δ = (m11 − m22)² + 4·m12·m21, eigenvalues (tr ± √Δ)/2 and null vectors of M − λI; irrational values evaluate the closed forms in double arithmetic; cross-checked against the rational oracle (tests/reference/oracles/linear-transformation.ts) within the declared tolerance

cases.label: Exact boundary: m22 one unit in the last place above 2 makes det = +2^-52, so the matrix is invertible and orientation is preserved, never collapsed
cases.rationale: From reference case near-singular-positive: hand derivation with the column-vector convention (M·e₁ is the first column): images, det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21, area |det M|, tr M, Δ = (m11 − m22)² + 4·m12·m21, eigenvalues (tr ± √Δ)/2 and null vectors of M − λI; det = 0.5·m22 − 1 is exactly 2^-52 for the stored m22 = 2 + 2^-51; eigenvalues λ₁ = (tr + √Δ)/2 and λ₂ = det/λ₁; directions perturb (1, 2)/√5 and (2, −1)/√5 by about 1e-16; cross-checked against the rational oracle within the declared tolerance

cases.label: Exact boundary: m22 one unit in the last place below 2 makes det = −2^-53, so the matrix is invertible and orientation is reversed, never collapsed
cases.rationale: From reference case near-singular-negative: hand derivation with the column-vector convention (M·e₁ is the first column): images, det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21, area |det M|, tr M, Δ = (m11 − m22)² + 4·m12·m21, eigenvalues (tr ± √Δ)/2 and null vectors of M − λI; det = 0.5·m22 − 1 is exactly −2^-53 for the stored m22 = 2 − 2^-52; eigenvalues λ₁ = (tr + √Δ)/2 and λ₂ = det/λ₁; directions perturb (1, 2)/√5 and (2, −1)/√5 by about 1e-16; cross-checked against the rational oracle within the declared tolerance

cases.label: Decimal entries [[0.1, 0.7], [0.3, 2.1]]: singular in decimal arithmetic, invertible as stored doubles (det ≈ 4.16e-17 > 0)
cases.rationale: From reference case decimal-near-singular: The decimal matrix is singular by hand (second column = 7 × first column). The determinant of the stored doubles is NOT hand-derived: it is the exact rational value of m11·m22 − m12·m21 for the stored entries computed by the rational oracle (tests/reference/oracles/linear-transformation.ts), which also fixes λ₂ = det/λ₁. The remaining values are hand closed forms of the decimal matrix (directions (1, 3)/√10 and (7, −1)/√50), within the declared tolerance of the stored-entry values

cases.label: Exact boundary of the repeated case: the shear with m21 = +2^-60 has Δ = 6·2^-60 > 0, two distinct real eigenvalues and two nearly parallel directions
cases.rationale: From reference case near-repeated-two-real: hand derivation with the column-vector convention (M·e₁ is the first column): images, det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21, area |det M|, tr M, Δ = (m11 − m22)² + 4·m12·m21, eigenvalues (tr ± √Δ)/2 and null vectors of M − λI; Δ = 4·1.5·2^-60 exactly; λ = 1 ± √1.5·2^-30; u = (1, ±t)/√(1 + t²) with t = 2^-30/√1.5; cross-checked against the rational oracle within the declared tolerance

cases.label: Exact boundary of the repeated case on the other side: m21 = −2^-60 gives Δ = −6·2^-60 < 0 and no real unchanged direction
cases.rationale: From reference case near-repeated-complex: hand derivation with the column-vector convention (M·e₁ is the first column): images, det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21, area |det M|, tr M, Δ = (m11 − m22)² + 4·m12·m21, eigenvalues (tr ± √Δ)/2 and null vectors of M − λI; Δ = −4·1.5·2^-60 exactly; det = 1 + 1.5·2^-60 rounds to 1; cross-checked against the rational oracle within the declared tolerance

cases.label: Tiny scalar matrix 2^-600·I: det = 2^-1200 is nonzero but below the smallest double, so it is an UNDERFLOW limit, never 0; orientation and rank still follow the exact value
cases.rationale: From reference case underflow-determinant: hand derivation with the column-vector convention (M·e₁ is the first column): images, det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21, area |det M|, tr M, Δ = (m11 − m22)² + 4·m12·m21, eigenvalues (tr ± √Δ)/2 and null vectors of M − λI; det = (2^-600)² = 2^-1200 < 2^-1075; cross-checked exactly against the rational oracle

cases.label: Small scalar matrix 2^-530·I: det = 2^-1060 is representable only as a subnormal double, so it is valid with an UNDERFLOW approximation note
cases.rationale: From reference case subnormal-determinant: hand derivation with the column-vector convention (M·e₁ is the first column): images, det M = m11·m22 − m12·m21, area |det M|, tr M, Δ = (m11 − m22)² + 4·m12·m21, eigenvalues (tr ± √Δ)/2 and null vectors of M − λI; det = (2^-530)² = 2^-1060, between 2^-1074 and 2^-1022; cross-checked exactly against the rational oracle

stages.instruction: Vectors are columns and M acts by M·v. The first column of M is where e₁ = (1, 0) lands and the second column is where e₂ = (0, 1) lands. The grid, the unit square, e₁, e₂, their images and the test vector v are shown; the transformed plane is not shown yet.
The arrows Me₁ and Me₂ are the columns of the matrix shown. Before the transformed plane is shown, predict what M does to the whole plane.

response.prompt: For this matrix, will M keep the counterclockwise order of e₁ and e₂, reverse it, or flatten the plane onto a line or a point? Which directions through the origin, if any, will M map onto their own line?

stages.instruction: Change the matrix entries or type exact values, and watch the transformed grid, the image of the unit square, Mv, the determinant and the area scale. Compare what you see with your prediction.
Now look for directions that M maps onto their own line through the origin. Compare matrices with two such directions, exactly one, every direction, and none.
Explain in your own words how the matrix entries determine orientation, area, collapse and the unchanged directions.

response.prompt: How do the columns of M and its determinant tell you whether orientation is kept or reversed, how areas scale and whether the plane collapses? When does a matrix have no real unchanged direction, exactly one, or every direction?
